idiom_name: one-method Authenticator interface + registry map + middleware; goth.Provider for federated flows
implementation_notes: The idiomatic realization is a single-method interface - Authenticate(ctx context.Context, creds Credentials) (Principal, error) - with implementations held in a map[string]Authenticator resolved by the scheme configured on the route; middleware calls it and stores the principal in the request context, so handlers see only the principal. Federated providers follow the same shape at library scale: goth lets any OAuth/OIDC provider implement its Provider and Session interfaces and register with gothic. The interface plus map replaces the classic abstract class, factory and dispatcher; the full class structure is unnecessary in Go. Transport-level verification (mutual TLS) belongs to the crypto/tls, crypto/x509 stack rather than to a hand-written authenticator.
pitfalls: Returning a nil error with a zero-value principal must never count as success; make every failure path return an error.
Storing credentials in context.Context is an anti-pattern; store only the resolved principal.
Verifiers must validate exp/nbf/aud/iss and pin the signing algorithm; JWT libraries happily accept alg=none when misused.
An interface value holding a typed nil (*X)(nil) passes nil checks and panics later; return an untyped nil error instead.
